text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
-- The cabinet decided on Thursday to amend the land law to allow all domestic legal entities to purchase land even if they have foreign owners.

-- The cabinet decided to spend 153 billion forints than 169 billion on centrally funded projects next year and allocate the remaining 16 billion forints to local governments and the interior and defense ministries.
-- Prime Minister Gyula Horn said that he expected NATO accession talks to start in September.

-- The Democratic Forum (MDF), the Christian Democrats (KDNP), the Young Democrats (Fidesz-MPP) and the Agricultural Producers Advocacy Organisation (Metesz) have joined an initiative to stage a referendum on land ownership.

-- Former leaders of the Smallholders' Party (FKGP) said that according to a letter presented to the current party president, Jozsef Torgyan by the then Prime Minister Jozsef Antall in 1991, Torgyan had been member of the communist secret service.
-- MTV president Istvan Petak can keep his job after more than one third of the Hungarian Television Board of Trustees voted in his favor in a secret ballot yesterday.

-- Arhangelszk Geologia Kft., the winner of the first tender aimed at selling off the oil exploration company Szolnoki Koolajkutato Rt., will sue the State Privatization & Holding Co. (APV Rt.), Arhangelszk executive director Zoltan Szakacs announced yesterday.
-- The bus maker NABI Rt. plans two share issues followed by a listing on the Budapest Stock Exchange.
-- A Czech-Hungarian-Slovak consortium yesterday founded Nova Hut Hungary Rt. to sell products of Nova Hut Ostrava, the Czech Republic's largest steelworks.
MAGYAR NEMZET

-- Prime Minister Gyula Horn, Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs and Foreign Ministry state secretary for integration affairs Ferenc Somogyi will represent Hungary at a meeting between EU leaders and the head of the associate states in Amsterdam today.
-- President Arpad Goncz met the leadership of the World Jewish Congress in New York Thursday, to discuss compensation issues and the state of affairs in Central Europe.
NEPSZABADSAG

-- The latest poll of Szonda-Ipsos shows the Socialists (MSZP) gaining in popularity, supported by 31 percent of decided voters, while the Young Democrats (Fidesz-MPP) are at second place with 22 percent.

-- The new Ft 10,000 note will be introduced to the press today and will be legal tender across Hungary from July 1. The banknote features a portrait of Hungary's first king, Saint Stephen, as drawn by graphic artist Karoly Vagyoczky.

-- Yesterday saw the temporary closure of the well-known downtown restaurants Amadeus and Cyrano, and Flashdance bar for various irregularities. Nine establishments have now been shut down since the infamous Dreher Halaszcsarda was found to be outrageously overcharging customers. VILAGGAZDASAG
-- The economic recovery continued in the spring months, according to the latest analysis by Postabank and the economic research company GKI.

-- The Scandinavian-led consortium MTM-SBS has put in the highest bid for a national TV channel concession, and that political differences prevented the National Radio and Television Board (ORTT) from awarding the other concession to the CME-led consortium at its Wednesday meeting.
NAPI GAZDASAG
-- Bids will be invited for 83.6% of Mezobank Rt. in a closed tender no later than July 31, according to a Thursday cabinet decision.

-- Several companies of strategic importance will not be privatized until the State Privatization & Holding Co. (APV Rt.) has been wound up sometime next year, APV managing director Pal Szabo told the press yesterday.
-- Budapest newsroom (36 1) 327 40 40
